source: same call site as kb-extract.json (engine/kb_extract.rs:167-203); prompt unchanged, documents harder
notes: HARD tier. Documents live in kb-extract-hard/*.txt (6.3-8.5k chars each, vs 0.3-0.5k in the easy tier). Each one plants, around facts buried mid-document: near-duplicate distractors with changed numbers or dates (a bid price vs the negotiated value, a superseded data sheet, a withdrawn estimate, a transposed certificate number), a NEGATED instance that must not become a row ('X was NOT adopted / NOT installed / NOT part of this incident'), and at least one fact split across two paragraphs or sections (the entity in one, its value later). The schema `description` carries the rule that decides which instances are real (awarded, installed, adopted, in force, currently valid), so every trap is decidable from the prompt alone. Checks are unchanged: factRecall, noInventedFacts (absentStrings on the lowercased rows JSON; absentPatterns as regexes on the whitespace-squashed, lowercased rows JSON), rowCounts. `traps` names what each `bad` sample (one per trap) falls for.
